evals.prompt: Photoreal Mount Rainier from Tacoma at golden hour, 1500x500, no AI image generator. I want to see how far pure code gets.
evals.expected_output: A ray-marched Rainier render lit on the camera-facing slopes, with haze and snow.
expectations: Looked up Rainier's summit and a Tacoma viewpoint
Ran scripts/pbr_terrain.py then scripts/post_terrain.py
Rendered a small draft and looked at it before the final
Sun lights the faces the camera sees (default or explicit --sun-az), not backlit
Checked the printed peak elevation against the real ~4392 m

evals.prompt: Mount Hood reflected in Trillium Lake, calm water, like the classic postcard, but rendered from scratch
evals.expected_output: A lake-reflection render of Mount Hood using the water features.
expectations: Used --water-level (a number near the lake surface, or auto) with low --waves for calm water
Placed the camera just above the lake near the shore
Reflection of the mountain is visible in the output
Mentioned limits honestly if trees near the camera look game-like at 1:1

evals.prompt: Salt Lake City lights at blue hour with the Wasatch behind, photographic
evals.expected_output: A blue-hour render with a city light field in front of the mountains.
expectations: Used --time blue (or night) with --city > 0
Chose a viewpoint west of the city looking east at the Wasatch
Kept the result honest: city reads as lights at a distance, not detailed streets

evals.prompt: Render a tumbler of whiskey with two ice cubes and a brass coaster on a dark walnut table, window light from the left. No Blender, just math.
evals.expected_output: A path-traced still life defined as a JSON scene (tube glass, liquid fill, box ice, metal disk).
expectations: Wrote a scene JSON rather than editing the renderer
Used a hollow tube (or glass with fill) for the tumbler and separate liquid, box primitives for ice
Ran low-spp drafts before adding samples to the same accumulator
Post-processed with post_pathtrace.py and presented the image

evals.prompt: turn this photo into an oil painting, and then also a watercolor version so I can compare
evals.expected_output: Two paintings of the provided image via paint.py (oil and watercolor) plus a comparison.
expectations: Ran scripts/paint.py --style oil and --style watercolor on the provided file
Presented both results side by side or as a comparison sheet
Did not use any image generation model

evals.prompt: Sunset timelapse of Kilimanjaro from Amboseli, 6 seconds, going from golden light into night
evals.expected_output: An MP4 timelapse made with timelapse.py.
expectations: Ran scripts/timelapse.py with a real Kilimanjaro summit and Amboseli viewpoint
Output is an MP4 of about 6 seconds
Rendered in resumable chunks that fit the shell time limit

evals.prompt: a prism splitting sunlight into a rainbow on white linen, super crisp, for my physics class slides
evals.expected_output: A path-traced prism scene with dispersion, based on the shipped prism scene or a new JSON.
expectations: Used a prism primitive with an abbe number for dispersion
Used a small, strong light (sun through a window) so the spectrum is sharp
Rendered at a slide-friendly size and presented it

evals.prompt: can you render a photoreal bouquet of roses in a vase using only code?
evals.expected_output: An honest answer about the limits for organic shapes, with a fitting alternative.
expectations: Explained that organic, irregular shapes like petals are a weak spot of these renderers
Offered an alternative that plays to the strengths (glass vase with water and simple forms, or a painterly finish)
